decisions.reason: Quotes profile-introspection.txt LinkType Junction with Target E:\dev\dsh-attach-input and the cordis.patch.yml link marker, concludes the repo tree IS the installed copy, states copying was never the right move for this mode, and contrasts a copied dependency install.

Attributes the EBUSY to the running dsh host holding the lib files so closing the browser tab released nothing, and separately explains browser caching of client.js; requires host restart plus a cache-bypassing refresh, without treating the cache as a filesystem lock or extrapolating to all DSH versions.

Explains the rename via the junction path renamed the sole source file so the later source copy found nothing; recovery stops the host, renames client.js.old2/index.js.old2 back to the original names in place, verifies both with node --check, and activates without copying or deleting the .old2 files.

Gives the correct order: fully stop the dsh host, restart it so the host re-reads lib/index.js and re-serves client.js, then hard-refresh to bypass the browser cache, then verify via Network/Sources and the new host route; notes browser-only restart is insufficient.

Prescribes checking Get-Item LinkType/Target on the profile entry plus the cordis.patch.yml link marker before any file operation, interprets empty LinkType as a copied install, and explains why generic copy-into-node_modules advice acts on the repo itself under a junction.

caps.reason: The final recovery/deployment plan explicitly requires no copy step and restores the .old2 files by renaming them back to their original names; the two paths are treated as one directory, so the cap's affirmative-advice condition is not met.
The plan requires fully stopping and restarting the dsh host for both lock release and making the edit effective; browser hard refresh is only for cache bypass, so the cap does not apply.
